note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Unilateral left-ear hearing loss for six weeks with intermittent tinnitus and mild dizziness; plan for in-clinic ear examination to exclude wax blockage and assess other causes; follow-up with GP in 4–5 days; tinnitus education provided.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Left-ear hearing deterioration for ~6 weeks; associated left-ear tinnitus and occasional dizziness.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began ~6 weeks ago; intermittent but ongoing.
- Associated symptoms: Ringing in left ear; occasional feeling of being off-balance; no ear pain, no discharge; no fever reported.
- Negative findings: Right ear hearing is reportedly fine; no chest pain or palpitations.
- Prior similar issue: One year ago had a brief hearing-related issue lasting a few days.
- PMH/medications/allergies: Not documented beyond prior ear issue; no medications or allergies stated.
- Social history/preventive care: Not documented.

Examination:
- Not performed in this transcript; no vitals or exam findings available.

Impression:
- Working impression: Unilateral left-ear hearing loss with tinnitus; tinnitus mechanism unclear; differential includes possible wax impaction and other inner-ear or middle-ear etiologies; no emergency identified at this time.

Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face ear examination with a GP at a clinic within 4–5 days to assess for wax blockage or other causes (otoscopic exam).
- Admin to slot appointment; patient to attend with notes from this visit.
- If wax blockage is found, treat accordingly; if not, proceed with further evaluation as indicated.
- Provide patient with tinnitus leaflet link in appointment notes; patient advised to read.
- If symptoms worsen or issues arise before the appointment, patient advised to book another appointment (video available).
- No medications prescribed at this time.
